issues.problem: Contexts 1 and 4 (problem harder than thought; old-house repair) could be filled just as well by 手に負えない from the same set.
issues.action: Rewrote ctx1 so the simple method (plugging into a formula) fails, and ctx4 so the repair is hard but finished in the end, which rules out 手に負えない.

issues.problem: Misuse 1 (heavy cardboard boxes) is not clearly wrong: 荷が重い can still be read literally. Context 5 (caring for a parent alone) fits 手に負えない equally. Context 1 used 私に where 私には is the natural form.
issues.action: Replaced misuse 1 with using it as a character trait of a responsible person. Rewrote ctx5 as being asked to chair the neighbourhood association. Changed 私に to 私には in ctx1.

issues.problem: Misuse 2 (いつも知恵を絞る人) is acceptable Japanese for 'someone who always thinks hard', so it is not clearly wrong.
issues.action: Replaced it with 後輩に知恵を絞ってあげた, meant as giving advice, which is 知恵を貸す.

issues.problem: Context 5 (finding a shared hobby on first meeting) is the typical situation for 話が合う, which is in the set.
issues.action: Rewrote ctx5 as club members chatting happily about manga when practice is rained off. Added 話が合う to near with the difference.

issues.problem: The reason given for misuse 1 said the phrase is figurative today, but the literal railway use still exists.
issues.action: Reworded it: it is never a normal departure, even literally, and is now mostly figurative.

issues.problem: Story checked: the alternating hammer strokes of smith and assistant (相鎚) are the standard etymology.
Story is null. The folk tales of the origin vary and are not certain.
